full_judgment:
7. After the close of the examination of the prosecution witnesses, the accused Yunus was examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to which he expressed his innocence and the defence did not adduce any evidence on his behalf. 

 9. On consideration of the evidence on record as well as the facts and circumstances of the case, the learned Special Tribunal No.2, Khulna was pleased to convict the accused appellants under section 25A, Special Powers Act, 1974 and sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10 years and to pay a fine of Taka 5000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6(six) months more by his judgment and order dated 16-9-2002. 

 11. Mr Sarwar Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the appellants, took us through FIR, charge sheet, charge so framed, the deposition of the prosecution witnesses and the impugned judgment and order and materials available in the paper books and submits, that the prosecution failed to prove the alleged recovery of counterfeit money from the possession of the accused appellants by reliable and independent witnesses and that the mandatory provisions of section 103 of the Code of Criminal Procedure have not been complied with in accordance with law. It is further submitted that investigation of the case is highly defective and doubtful; that there are major contradictions amongst the evidence of prosecution witnesses on material points; that the provisions of section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure have not been complied with in accordance with law and that the judgment and order dated 16-9-2002 passed by the learned Special Tribunal Judge, Court No.2 is bad in law as well as on facts and, as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. 

 13. Mr SM Shajahan Kabir, learned Assistant Attorney-General for State, on the other hand, submits that the prosecution proved its case against the accused appellants by most consistent, corroborative and overwhelming evidence of competent witnesses. He further submits that the learned Special Tribunal Judge was perfectly justified in convicting and sentencing the accused appellants on the basis of the most cogent and reliable evidence and his judgment does not suffer from any misreading and non-reading of evidence. He further submits that all the prosecution witnesses are natural, probable and competent witnesses and there is no internal points of falsehood in their evidence on any point and, as such, the impugned judgment calls for no interference by the Court. 

 16. In the face of argument advanced by the learned Advocates of the contending parties, we are now called upon to scrutinise the material evidence in order to come to a proper decision in this appeal. 

 38. These are all the evidence adduced by the prosecution. 

 49. To meet the argument of the learned Advocate for the appellant, we may refer the law and decision regarding seizure of articles which is envisaged in the section 103 of the Code of Criminal Procedure: 

 103: Search to be made in presence of witnesses (1) Before making a search under this chapter, the offender or other person about to make it shall call upon two or more respectable inhabitants of the locality in which the place to be searched is situate to attend and witness the search and may issue an order in writing to them or any of them so to do. 

 50. In the instant case, the compliance of the provision of section 103 regarding seizure was followed. The forged currency notes were recovered from the pocket of the accused persons in presence of 3 local witnesses beside police personnel. PW 9 Fakir Fariduzzaman and PW 9 Dr Md Azizur Rahman are local seizure list witnesses who substantially deposed that Khondaker Md Iqbal Assistant Police Super, CID, Khulna prepared seizure list in their presence recovering the forged currency notes from the accused Yunus Ali and Shawkat. PW 1 Khondaker Md Iqbal proves the seizure list which is marked as Exhibit-I. 

 51. On reading of evidence of police witnesses, it appears to us that they after seizing the forged currency notes, arrested accused persons who were thereafter brought to the Kotwali police station. 

 52. There is no legal bar to convict and sentence the accused under Special Power Act mainly on the evidence of police personnel if there appears no falsehood in their evidence. Thus we do not find any bar to convict the accused Yunus Ali and Shawkat on the basis of unimpeachable evidence of the police witnesses who made the search and prepared the seizure list. The above view finds support in the case of Nurul Islam vs State reported in 1988 BLD 106. 

 53. The object of the provisions of section 103, CrPC is to ensure conducting of search in an impartial way and fair manner and also ensure that there is no planting of incriminating articles by the police or by any other person. There are quite a number of cases where the local witnesses of search and seizure do not support the police out of fear of the accused and their men or on being gained over or for various other reasons depose falsely in favour of the accused to save the offender from legal punishment. Depending on the facts and circumstances of each case, a judge certainly may disbelieve a witness of search and seizure if it appears to him that he is deliberately making obliging statements in favour of the accused falsely in order to save him from legal punishment. In view of the provision of section 134 of the Evidence Act which provides that no particular number of witnesses shall in any case be required for the proof of any fact. A Judge may convict an accused solely on the basis of the unimpeachable an unshaken evidence of the officer or person who made the search and seizure disbelieving the evidence, if any, of any witnesses of search and seizure holding it to be unworthy of credit. But in the present case, the reasons stated above, it appears to us, that the witnesses of search and seizure namely PW 1 Khondaker Md Iqbal, PW 2, SI Abdur Rahim and PW 3 constable No. 63 Motiur Rahman, PW 9, Fakir Fariduzzaman and PW 11 Dr Azizur Rahman categorically deposed that the forged currency were recovered from the accused persons through seizure list prepared in their presence in which they were also witnesses. Even if the seizure list witnesses do not support the prosecution case, the conviction and sentence under section 25A of the Special Powers Act, 1974 can be awarded solely on the testimonies of the police personnel. 

 55. The purpose of examination under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is to facilitate the accused to explain the evidence against him. 

 56. In the instant case, the accused appellants are sufficiently intellectual men and they are well aware of the fact of recovery of forged currency notes from them. They remaining present in the dock and heard of evidence adduced by the witnesses against them and such evidence was not even challenged during cross examination. In this case, detailed narration of the evidence is not necessary as because the facts and evidence are within knowledge of the accused persons. So there is no chance of being prejudiced by the accused Yunus Ali and Shakwat Hossain. 

 57. It is not fact that the accused persons were not examined under section 342 of the Code. Moreover, the evidence placed before the accused persons are sufficient for them to understand the nature of accusation brought against them. We do not find any noncompliance of the provision of section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and thus the accused appellants have not been prejudiced. 

 Secondly, whether such deception has been practised. Thirdly, whether the forged currency notes have been received and seized properly, and whether such recovery has been proved by sufficient evidence. 

 60. On a meticulous survey of evidence, browsing materials on record and considering facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the considered view that all the above mentioned ingredients have been found against the appellants. The accused appellants had committed so serious offence which will jeopardise the economy of Bangladesh, so they deserve punishment. 

 61. On bestowing our dispassionate consideration ofthe evidence, materials on record and striking features of the case, we can safely come to the conclusion that prosecution has succeeded in proving its case against convict appellants beyond any shadow of doubt.
